question: A piece of furniture is marked at 35% above its cost price. The shopkeeper gives a discount of 18% on the marked price and still earns ₹1,498 profit. What is the cost price of the furniture?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net profit percentage = **a + b + (ab ÷ 100)** where a is **markup** and b is **discount** (negative).

Profit% = 35 − 18 − (35 × 18 ÷ 100) = 17 − 6.3 = **10.7%**.

Given 10.7% of CP = 1,498.

1% of CP = 1,498 ÷ 10.7 = 140.

100% of CP = 140 × 100 = **14,000**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹14,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Markup % = 35%**, **Discount % = 18%**, **Profit = ₹1,498**.
Formulas: MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100 | Profit = SP − CP.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/47377e0ac520e9d80e233db89fe886e4cb5680ca003743cfc6af601db3ec82a6.png] 
⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** = 100 units.
⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 35% of 100 = 135 units.
⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 135 − 18% of 135 = 135 − 24.3 = 110.7 units.
⇒ **Profit** = SP − CP = 110.7 − 100 = 10.7 units.
⇒ 10.7 units = ₹1,498.
⇒ 1 unit = 1498 ÷ 10.7 = 140.
⇒ 100 units = 140 × 100 = ₹14,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹14,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. Relationship: SP = MP × (100 − D%)/100.

Markup Percentage

Markup is the increase in price over the **Cost Price (CP)**. Relationship: MP = CP × (100 + Markup%)/100.
